name: permit-tracker-permit
title: Permit
description: One permit: a timeline of submittal, agency review rounds, issuance and expiry read from its status history (Change status logs each step); what the application needs and which permits it waits on; the permit file; the full status history; and how long this permit usually takes at this agency. Each editable section opens its own side drawer.

guide.intent: The permit's history with the agency (submittal, each review round, issuance, expiry) read from its status log, with a pace badge comparing it with the typical time for this permit type at this agency.
decisions: Dates are never typed in: they come from status changes (Change status logs the change, its date and a note; an issued status also takes the expiry).

Pace: Took longer than typical / Within typical time once issued; Taking longer than typical once past the median; Likely to take longer when the remaining review rounds, at the rate so far, project past 115% of the median (the Issued step then shows the projected date).
acceptance: Changing status to Issued with an expiry adds both to the timeline and updates the project's readiness.

guide.intent: The application checklist (the permit type's standard items plus custom ones), then the permits this one waits on and the permits that wait on it, each with its status.
decisions: Checking an item off stamps who and when; items can be edited, and custom ones removed.
Waits on is edited in its own drawer; a plain note says the permit cannot be submitted until its unissued prerequisites are issued.
acceptance: Removing every Waits on entry shows None and drops the blocked note, and the project's list stops flagging "Waiting on".

Process
City of Bellevue reviews critical areas with the underlying land use or development permit. Work that needs no other permit is reviewed on its own as an administrative decision.
When review applies
Applies to development within or near a wetland, stream, geologically hazardous area or their buffers. A critical areas report by a qualified professional is required when one is present or likely.

guide.intent: What the permit's type says in general (level, how long it stays valid, typical days across agencies, governing law) and at this permit's agency (typical days there; for Critical Areas Review the agency's ordinance with its last amendment, the rules' review status, and the gist of the rules), each linking to its Permit types page.
decisions: Rules status badges: AI suggested, Edited (not validated), Validated; plus Example data for template content and Ordinance changed when the code was amended after the rules were last reviewed.
It reads the same stores as the Permit types pages, so edits there show here.
acceptance: "Full rules and buffer tables for <agency>" opens that agency's Critical Areas Review page.
